Definition: from G782; a greeting (in person or by letter):--greeting, salutation.
BiblicalUsage: A greeting in the ancient world was more than politeness, and this word carries its weight in both directions. Mary was troubled at Gabriel's greeting, Elizabeth's child leaped when she heard Mary's, the Pharisees loved greetings in the marketplaces, and Paul signed his own greeting at the end of his letter to Corinth.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a greeting shows what a person is reaching for, whether it is honour from men or grace from God. Mary's greeting carried the Saviour Himself into Elizabeth's house, and I hold that the simplest hello can carry Christ with it.
RelatedPeople: Mary, Mother of Jesus; Jesus; Paul
